caption: Focus on neighboring cells to narrow down the candidates.
content: When you place a tile on a cell, it restricts which tiles can be placed on the neighboring cells. Using this, you can narrow down the candidate tiles.

content.caption: Example
content: Assuming your available tiles are @t{forest_road.2s.lr} @t{forest_road.2t.dr} @t{forest_open.1.dr} and their rotations, let's solve this Area.
First, if we focus on the cell @m{pending}, there are two tiles that can be placed here: @t{forest_road.2s.lr} @t{forest_road.2t.dl}.
If we place @t{forest_road.2s.lr}, there will be no available tiles we can place on the cell @m{unsatisfied}.
Therefore, we place @t{forest_road.2t.dl} on the cell @m{pending}.
Next, if we focus on the cell @m{pending}, there are two tiles that can be placed here: @t{forest_road.2t.dl} @t{forest_open.1.dl}.
If we place @t{forest_open.1.dl}, there will be no available tiles for the cell @m{unsatisfied}.
Therefore, we place @t{forest_road.2t.dl} on the cell @m{pending}.
From here, if you consider the @g{tips/complete_block/common/candidate_1}{candidate tiles for the remaining cells}, you'll complete the Area.
